title: Noetherian finite scalar-model constructible heart for all coefficient cases
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda$ be one of $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$, discrete for $A$ and norm-topological otherwise. Its condensed ring is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$ on profinite sets [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], set $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal A_X=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$ be the ordinary uncompleted internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\mathcal C_X$ be its full replete subcategory of finite constant scalar-model constructible modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; in particular finitely presented integral torsion scalar models are allowed. Then $\mathcal C_X$ is essentially small in the specified indexing universe, contains zero, and is closed in $\mathcal A_X$ under kernels and cokernels of all maps between its objects and under every ambient extension. Thus it is an abelian category with exact inclusion. No condition on the characteristic or dimension of $X$ is imposed; the empty scheme and zero coefficient ring are included.

source.place: Theorem 6.2(3), Lemma 6.10, Corollary 6.11 and the finite scalar-model interpretation of the heart; discrete Noetherian coefficients: Stacks Tags 09B5 and 03RZ. Essential smallness follows from small-site finite descent data. Agent formulation combining the coefficient cases; no claim about arbitrary non-Noetherian schemes.

proof.text: Work in the ordinary ambient abelian category: [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies internal modules with sectionwise module sheaves, and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] supplies its abelian structure on the fixed small site. By [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], every finite constant scalar model is locally finitely presented. Thus each object of $\mathcal C_X$ lies in the essentially small class of [lem-sfb-constructible-module-objects-essentially-small], applied to the ring object $\Lambda_X$ and our quasi-compact locally Noetherian $X$. Take the subfamily of its small representatives satisfying our scalar-model predicate. Repleteness makes this a small representative family for $\mathcal C_X$, in exactly the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. This implication only uses scalar-model implies local finite presentation, never its false converse.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph; restrict the existing local-finite-presentation small family to finite scalar-model objects

proof.text: Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated; together with the assumed quasi-compactness this permits the global finite-stratification convention. The underlying space of $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Every subspace is Noetherian: an increasing chain of relative opens is represented by ambient opens, whose successive finite unions give a stabilizing increasing ambient chain. Consequently every locally closed stratum is topologically Noetherian, and [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] gives finitely many irreducible components on it and on its open subspaces. For any pair of constructible objects take the finite common stratification formed by fibre products in [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection]. Finite scalar models persist on a further restriction: pull back the scalar finite matrix presentation of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]; the exact pullback of [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] preserves its cokernel and finite free terms, with the same scalar entries. The composition comparisons of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identify this with restriction from $X$. Thus both objects have finite scalar models on every common stratum. Exactness also identifies restrictions of ambient kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences with those computed on the stratum.

source.place: Theorem 6.2 proof, restriction to strata and their finite-component hypothesis; scalar-matrix refinement argument

proof.text: First treat $\Lambda\in\{\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$. Every field has only the ideals $0$ and the unit ideal. The valuation rings here are principal ideal domains by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] for $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] for $\mathcal O_E$. In a domain multiplication by a nonzero generator identifies any nonzero principal ideal with the free rank-one module; the zero ideal is projective too. Hence all finitely generated ideals of each of the five scalar rings are projective. Their norm topologies are metric, so singletons are closed. Apply [lem-sfb-semihereditary-topological-coefficients-admissible] to obtain regular coherence and flatness over every extremally disconnected profinite set. These are precisely the two hypotheses required in [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations], including for $C(-,\Omega)$ with all continuous functions. This argument imposes no finite-subextension or completeness condition on $\Omega$.

source.place: Lemma 6.10 and Corollary 6.11(1), fields and discrete valuation rings; Theorem 6.2(2) hypotheses

proof.text: On a common stratum $T$, take the full dualizable subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$. It is strictly full and triangulated by [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models]. The finite-component condition proved in step 2 and the coefficient hypotheses of step 3 permit [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations]: all standard truncations stay dualizable, and its degree-zero objects are exactly the finite constant scalar models. In particular its cohomology objects, placed in degree zero, are again dualizable. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-degree-zero-abelian-criterion] to this full triangulated subcategory. It follows that finite scalar models on $T$ contain zero and are closed under all ambient kernels, cokernels and extensions. Concretely, for a map of models, the two cohomology sheaves of its dualizable cone give its kernel and cokernel; for an ambient short exact sequence its triangle and closure under cones give the middle model. These statements apply to integral torsion models as well as finite free field models. By step 2 every restriction of an ambient kernel, cokernel or extension of constructible sheaves has this form on the finite common stratification. That stratification therefore witnesses constructibility of the resulting sheaf, by [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

source.place: Definition 3.3 and stability observation; Theorem 6.2(2)-(3); ordinary derived degree-zero closure criterion

proof.text: For the remaining case $\Lambda=A$, [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] gives an exact equivalence between $\mathcal A_X$ and the category of ordinary module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$. An exact equivalence of abelian categories preserves and reflects kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. Since $X$ is Noetherian and $A$ is a finite commutative ring, [lem-pe-finite-coefficient-model-comparison] shows that a $\Lambda_X$-module lies in $\mathcal C_X$ if and only if its image is constructible in the locally constant finite-stalk sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. The same finite constructible stratifications serve, and the comparison supplies both the finiteness of the stalks and the converse passage from finite locally constant values back to finitely presented scalar models. Let $f$ be a morphism in $\mathcal C_X$, or let $0\to M\to L\to N\to0$ be an ambient short exact sequence with $M,N\in\mathcal C_X$. Apply [lem-weil-proetale-constructible-exact-closure] to the image under the equivalence: the images of $\ker f$, $\operatorname{coker}f$ and $L$ are constructible in that sense. By the comparison again, $\ker f$, $\operatorname{coker}f$ and $L$ belong to $\mathcal C_X$. No regularity or finite projective dimension of $A$ is used. In particular $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ is handled here, not by the topological t-admissibility argument; the empty scheme and $A=0$ are included in both cited statements.

source.place: Tag 09B5 (lemma-constructible-serre), using Tag 03RZ (lemma-constructible-abelian)(3); finite scalar encoding

proof.text: The zero scalar module gives a zero object of $\mathcal C_X$ on the one-stratum stratification, also when $X$ is empty or $A=0$. The preceding two cases prove ambient kernel, cokernel and extension closure for every permitted coefficient. Finite biproducts belong to $\mathcal C_X$ by applying extension closure to the split sequence $0\to F\to F\oplus G\to G\to0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-full-subcategory-exact] to the full replete subcategory $\mathcal C_X\subseteq\mathcal A_X$: it is abelian with the ambient kernels and cokernels, and its inclusion is exact. Together with step 1 this gives every asserted clause. The only conditions on $X$ used were local Noetherianity and quasi-compactness; there was no dimension or characteristic restriction.
